subject: Geo authorization handoff & iptables scoping for private deploy
messages:
From: Emma O'Reilly <emma.oreilly@nordicbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andre Mori <andre.mori@kiri-cloud.com>
Date: 2028-02-09T09:14:00Z
Subject: Geo auth handoff and IP scoping for private deploy

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We have a short list of items the security and network teams at Nordic need clarified before we sign the Dedicated Private deployment SOW:

- How do you guarantee that user data processed for EU accounts never transits via APAC compute nodes during failover?
- We need the exact IP ranges (or ASNs) that Redwood will egress from for: primary EU region, warm-standby APAC region, and any peering hops.
- Any iptables / NAT rules you apply inside customer VPCs — will those be documented and auditable? Our auditors want a sample policy.
- Retention/forwarding of audit logs across regions (specifically: can logs be kept in EU-only storage).

Can you answer in writing and attach sample network diagrams + a minimal iptables rule set that we can feed to our infra auditors? We also want to lock down an on-site architecture review next Tuesday (Feb 14) if possible.

Cheers,
Emma
Emma O'Reilly
Head of Cloud Security, Nordic Bank
emma.oreilly@nordicbank.com
+44 7700 900123

Attachment: nordicbank-data-retention-requirements-2028.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emma O'Reilly <emma.oreilly@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-09T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Geo auth handoff and IP scoping for private deploy

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below and attached a network diagram and an example iptables diff file. More detail follows.

Short answers (high level):
- Data path guarantees: Redwood Private can be configured with region-pin routing for tenant keys; we provide a control-plane policy that prevents reads/writes from being routed to warm-standby APAC unless you explicitly enable cross-region failover. The warm-standby APAC nodes only receive encrypted replication traffic (metadata-only) unless you invoke failover.
- IP ranges: see attachment `redwood-network-diagram-v2.png` and the table in the doc. There are three blocks: EU-egress (10.240.48.0/20 used in the example deployment), APAC-warm (10.241.0.0/20), and peering VLAN ranges for partner exchanges. We will give you the public NAT ranges and cloud provider ASNs in the formal network appendix.
- iptables: we attach `iptables-scope-sample.diff` — it's a minimal, auditable set we apply when we manage a VPC appliance. It is deterministic and versioned.
- Audit logs: by default we ship audit logs to the customer's object storage endpoint. Policy can be configured to keep logs in EU-only buckets; we support customer-managed retention via lifecycle rules and can offer an EU-only KMS key.

Detailed notes: see the attached diagram for a typical VPC peering + transit topology. Key controls you asked for:
1) Role-based control-plane: only your operator IAM role + our on-call service account can trigger regional failover; those actions are logged and require two approvals for production tenants.
2) Network egress lock: the private dataplane runs in a VPC appliance in your account. We do not advertise Redwood-owned public IPs into your VPC — NATing happens in your subnets and we publish the precise prefixes we will use so you can create ACLs.
3) Iptables hygiene: the attached diff shows that we DROP by default, ALLOW only established connections, and explicitly allow ranges for control-plane health checks.

Next steps: Vivek can share the exact NAT/public ranges and a short blast of iptables that your auditors can run against a staging instance. If Tuesday (Feb 14) works, we will come on-site with the diagram and a readout. If you prefer remote, we can do a pre-recorded walkthrough.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram-v2.png, iptables-scope-sample.diff
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma O'Reilly <emma.oreilly@nordicbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-09T13:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Geo auth handoff and IP scoping for private deploy

Emma — adding operational constraints from the Dedicated deployment side:

- Canary policy: we will require a staged canary for any cross-region failover that involves live traffic. The default policy is `manual` for failover; auto failover is off unless explicitly requested in the SOW.
- SLA implications: cross-region failover involves cache warmup and KV replication; we estimate a 2–8 minute ramp depending on sequence length distributions. We will include this as an operational note in the runbook.
- Approvals: per Jordan, two approvers (your on-call + a Redwood deployment engineer) are required to trigger production cross-region failover. For the on-site review we should also cover the rollback plan — Vivek, please paste a short fence/rollback snippet you recommend for iptables and route priorities.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Emma O'Reilly <emma.oreilly@nordicbank.com>
Date: 2028-02-09T15:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Geo auth handoff and IP scoping for private deploy

On Thu, Feb 9, 2028 at 13:18, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Laura — adding operational constraints from the Dedicated deployment side:
> ...

Emma — attaching the small iptables example inline for quick review. This is the minimal fence we apply as a hot-standby policy before we flip traffic:

--- begin snippet ---
# assume managed appliance in customer subnet; default policy DROP
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT

# allow established flows
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# allow control-plane health checks from control IP ranges (EU control)
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.240.240.0/28 -p tcp --dport 8084 -j ACCEPT

# allow peering VLAN from vendor exchange (limited)
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.250.0.0/24 -j ACCEPT

# explicit drop for APAC warm-standby public ranges unless failover flag set
# (this is enforced by route advertisement in the appliance)
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.241.0.0/16 -j DROP
--- end snippet ---

Rollback snippet (simplified):
iptables -D INPUT -s 10.241.0.0/16 -j DROP  # remove APAC block so warm nodes can accept traffic again
# update route priorities: write priority=100 back to EU route table

I'll prepare the public NAT prefixes and ASNs in a separate doc tonight and upload to the Confluence link Jordan listed. We can also generate a CSV of the exact public egress IPs for your auditors.

- Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Emma O'Reilly <emma.oreilly@nordicbank.com>

Thank you — that level of detail is helpful. Quick confirmations: 

- Tuesday on-site works; we'll schedule the architecture review for Feb 14, 10:00 CET. I'll invite our network auditor and the SRE lead.
- Please upload the public NAT IP list and ASN table to the Confluence page and drop the CSV for the auditors before EOD Monday.
- We'll include the sample iptables snippet in the audit packet; the auditors want the iptables diff and the network diagram as separate files (already attached in your message, thanks).
- We'll also send a short security questionnaire specific to cross-border failover; expect it in the morning. If the BAA needs signing, we'll route DocuSign for the BAA after the review.

Best,
Emma
